value_chain.value_chain_position: GPU-specialized cloud infrastructure layer. CoreWeave sits between NVIDIA (its sole GPU supplier and major investor) and AI model creators/enterprises above. Unlike hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) that offer broad general-purpose cloud services, CoreWeave focuses exclusively on GPU compute for AI training and inference workloads. It serves the largest AI labs directly: Microsoft (62% of 2024 revenue), OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic, Cohere, Mistral, and IBM. CoreWeave is NVIDIA's preferred neocloud deployment partner, often receiving early access to new hardware (GB200 NVL72, forthcoming CPUs). It does not create models or provide application-layer services -- it is purely an infrastructure-as-a-service GPU cloud, making it a critical but single-layer player in the AI value chain.

key_products: GPU Cloud Compute (IaaS): on-demand and reserved GPU instances featuring NVIDIA H100, H200, and GB200 Blackwell chips across 32+ data centers in the US and Europe. CoreWeave was among the first to deploy NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 rack-scale systems at scale. Customers rent GPU clusters for AI model training and inference on a usage-based or long-term contract basis. The platform is purpose-built for AI workloads with high-performance networking (InfiniBand), low-latency storage, and Kubernetes-native orchestration.

Managed Kubernetes & AI Infrastructure: CoreWeave's platform runs on Kubernetes, offering customers a cloud-native API for provisioning and managing GPU clusters. Includes managed storage, networking, and MLOps tooling optimized for large-scale distributed training. Integrates with NVIDIA's full software stack (CUDA, NeMo, Triton Inference Server).

European Sovereign AI Cloud: $2.2B investment in data centers across the UK, Norway, Sweden, and Spain, powered by 100% renewable energy. Designed to meet EU data sovereignty requirements, providing localized AI infrastructure for European customers under GDPR and EU AI Act compliance frameworks.

business.revenue_or_valuation: FY2024 revenue: $1.92B (up from $229M in FY2023, +740% YoY). Q3 2025 revenue: $1.365B (+134% YoY). First 9 months of 2025: $3.6B (+204% YoY). FY2025 guidance: $5.05-5.15B. FY2026 analyst forecast: ~$12.1B. Market cap: ~$45B (Feb 2026). IPO priced at $40/share (March 28, 2025, NASDAQ: CRWV), stock trading ~$90 as of Feb 2026.
business.annual_recurring_revenue_arr: Not a traditional SaaS ARR model, but CoreWeave's long-term contracted backlog provides ARR-like visibility. Revenue backlog: $55.6B as of Q3 2025 (nearly doubled from Q2 2025). Contracted remaining performance obligation provides multi-year revenue visibility. FY2025 run rate based on Q3: ~$5.5B annualized. Key contracts: Meta up to $22.4B total, OpenAI $12B+ multi-year, Microsoft significant but declining as a share.
business.funding_total_and_last_round: Over $25B raised in total equity and debt financing. IPO (March 2025): raised $1.5B at $40/share, OpenAI concurrently bought $350M. Pre-IPO: Series C (Nov 2024) $650M at $23B valuation, Series B (Aug-Dec 2023) $2.35B at ~$7B valuation. NVIDIA invested $100M in April 2023 (Series B). NVIDIA invested additional $2B in January 2026 at $87.20/share (bringing stake to 11.5%). Debt: ~$14B total as of Q3 2025, including $7.6B facility at ~11% average rate, $2.6B secured facility, and $2.25B convertible notes. Additional $2.6B facility closed late 2025.
business.business_model: Usage-based GPU cloud rental (per-GPU-hour pricing) combined with long-term reserved capacity contracts. Customers pay for GPU compute time, typically on reserved multi-year contracts (enabling the $55.6B backlog) or on-demand. Pricing varies by GPU model (H100, H200, GB200) and market demand. Revenue is almost entirely infrastructure rental -- no software/application revenue. Adjusted EBITDA margin ~61% in Q3 2025 ($838M on $1.365B revenue), but net losses persist due to massive depreciation and interest expenses on $14B+ debt.
business.burn_rate_and_runway: Q3 2025 net loss: $110M (improved from $360M loss in Q3 2024). Free cash flow burn: ~$8B over trailing 12 months due to massive capex ($1.9B in Q3 alone). Total debt: $14B with $9.7B due within 12 months as of Sept 2025. Cash and equivalents: $3B as of Sept 2025. 2025 capex guidance: $12-14B. 2026 capex: 'well in excess of double' 2025 levels. Debt carries steep interest (9% unsecured notes, ~11% on main facility). Runway depends on continued ability to raise debt and equity -- high leverage is the primary financial risk.

openness.open_vs_closed_spectrum: Closed. CoreWeave is a proprietary cloud infrastructure provider. Its GPU cloud platform, networking stack, and orchestration layer are all proprietary. No open-source model or software contributions of note. Customers can run any open-source or closed AI frameworks on CoreWeave hardware, but the platform itself is closed. NVIDIA's CUDA ecosystem is the underlying software dependency.

startup_relevance.relevance_for_startups: CoreWeave is a critical case study for entrepreneurs in two ways -- as a potential infrastructure provider and as a business model example. Key considerations: (1) CoreWeave demonstrates that specialized infrastructure companies can compete with hyperscalers by focusing on a single use case (GPU compute for AI) rather than trying to offer everything, a lesson applicable to many vertical SaaS/infrastructure plays; (2) for AI startups needing large GPU clusters for training, CoreWeave offers an alternative to AWS/Azure/GCP with potentially faster provisioning and more GPU-optimized infrastructure, though long-term contract commitments may be required; (3) CoreWeave's meteoric rise (from crypto mining to $45B market cap in 8 years) shows the power of timing a platform shift -- they pivoted from Ethereum mining to AI cloud in 2022 just as generative AI exploded; (4) the $55.6B backlog from Meta, OpenAI, and Microsoft validates that even the largest tech companies need specialized GPU cloud beyond their own data centers; (5) however, CoreWeave's $14B debt load and ~$8B annual cash burn illustrate the capital intensity of infrastructure businesses -- this model requires massive upfront investment before profitability; (6) the heavy customer concentration (62% from Microsoft in 2024) is a risk factor that entrepreneurs should recognize in their own businesses; (7) for European startups, CoreWeave's $2.2B European expansion with sovereign cloud capabilities offers an alternative to US hyperscalers for GDPR-compliant AI training.
startup_relevance.accessibility: Accessible but primarily for larger AI workloads. CoreWeave targets enterprises and AI labs needing significant GPU capacity, not individual developers or small teams. Pricing is competitive with hyperscaler GPU instances but requires direct engagement for large deployments. No public free tier or startup credit program comparable to AWS Activate or Google for Startups. Long-term reserved capacity contracts (which form the bulk of the backlog) typically involve multi-year commitments of millions to billions of dollars. Smaller customers can access on-demand GPU instances, but CoreWeave's value proposition is strongest for organizations needing 100+ GPUs for distributed training. Not the right fit for a bootstrapped startup's first MVP.
startup_relevance.primary_model_dependency: None. CoreWeave is infrastructure-only and does not depend on any specific foundation model. Its customers bring their own models or build on open-source frameworks. However, CoreWeave is deeply dependent on NVIDIA hardware and CUDA ecosystem -- virtually all its GPUs are NVIDIA, and NVIDIA is both its primary supplier and largest strategic investor (11.5% stake).

ecosystem.key_partnerships: NVIDIA: deepest partnership -- $2B investment (Jan 2026, 11.5% stake), $100M initial investment (2023), $6B+ in committed NVIDIA services through 2032, early access to GB200 Blackwell and forthcoming CPUs/storage systems, goal of 5GW+ AI compute capacity by 2030. Microsoft: largest customer (62% of 2024 revenue), significant cloud infrastructure provider for Microsoft's AI workloads. OpenAI: $12B+ multi-year infrastructure deal, $350M equity purchase at IPO, $2.6B dedicated debt facility for OpenAI infrastructure. Meta: up to $22.4B in total commitments across expanded multi-year deals. IBM: partnership to build NVIDIA GB200-powered AI supercomputer for Granite models. Cohere: joint multibillion-dollar data center in Canada. Mistral AI: early customer for GB200 NVL72 systems.
ecosystem.competitive_moat: NVIDIA's preferred neocloud partner with early access to newest hardware generations (GB200, forthcoming CPUs) unavailable to competitors simultaneously. The $55.6B contracted backlog provides multi-year revenue visibility that no other neocloud can match. Purpose-built GPU infrastructure (InfiniBand networking, AI-optimized storage) offers performance advantages over hyperscaler GPU instances that were retrofitted into general-purpose clouds. Deep relationships with the three largest AI spenders (Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI) create reference customer effects. First-mover advantage in the neocloud category with the most data center capacity (32+ facilities, 250K+ GPUs). However, moat is narrower than hyperscalers: no proprietary software ecosystem, high debt leverage, customer concentration risk, and ultimate dependency on NVIDIA supply allocation.

regulatory.regulatory_exposure: Exempt as cloud infrastructure provider under EU AI Act -- CoreWeave hosts GPU compute but does not develop, deploy, or distribute AI models, placing it outside GPAI provider and deployer obligations. European data centers (UK, Norway, Sweden, Spain) are designed for EU data sovereignty compliance with GDPR-compliant infrastructure. No direct EU DMA gatekeeper risk given its small market share relative to hyperscalers. US regulatory exposure is minimal as a pure infrastructure provider. Primary regulatory risks are financial: SEC reporting obligations as a public company (NASDAQ: CRWV since March 2025), debt covenant compliance given $14B+ leverage, and energy/permitting regulations for rapid data center expansion.
